qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (3a=None, 3b=N, REJECT). Professional engineering consulting and infrastructure services operate in competitive bidding environments with sub-hurdle multi-cycle ROIC (<8% vs 12% requirement) and limited pricing power over consultant wage inflation.
qualitative.evidence: AtkinsRealis (formerly SNC-Lavalin) has historical multi-cycle ROIC well below 12% (1-8% range) due to legacy lump-sum turnkey project write-downs and competitive bidding on engineering consulting contracts. Even with the pivot to higher-margin nuclear and consulting services, capital returns fail the Munger moat standard.

qualitative.3m: Specialized engineering know-how, BIM prefabrication capabilities, deep relationships with general contractors and facility owners, and the largest aggregate pool of scarce skilled craft labor (union electrical and mechanical trades) in North America. While 5-year median ROIC is high (~19.5% historical median, spiking during the AI data center buildout), this capital efficiency is mathematically driven by an asset-light negative working capital model rather than pricing power. Operating margins historically averaged 4-6%, proving that pricing power cannot be sustained above inflation across the full business cycle without volume loss or competitive substitution.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). EMCOR is an exceptionally well-run specialty electrical and mechanical contractor currently enjoying peak-cycle earnings and record margins (~10%) from hyperscale AI data centers and reshoring mega-projects. However, specialty contracting lacks a structural, cycle-neutral economic moat. Work is won via competitive bidding or negotiated GMP/cost-plus contracts where bargaining power remains with facility owners and general contractors. Outside of cyclical supply crunches for skilled trades, operating margins historically average 4-6%, proving that pricing power cannot be sustained above inflation across the full business cycle without volume loss or competitive substitution.
qualitative.evidence: Revenues grew from $6.7B in FY15 to $14.6B in FY24 and over $15B in FY25. Consolidated operating margins averaged 4.0%-5.8% from 2014-2020 before expanding to 9.2% in FY24 and 10.1% in FY25, propelled by the unprecedented surge in hyperscale data center, semiconductor fab, and industrial cleanroom construction. High ROIC is primarily an artifact of an asset-light balance sheet with negative invested capital funded by customer advance billings. Contracts are project-based where building owners routinely solicit competing bids from regional and national MEP peers.

qualitative.3m: Premier mechanical and electrical contractor specializing in HVAC, plumbing, and modular off-site prefabrication for data centers, industrial plants, and healthcare. Off-site modular manufacturing provides substantial labor productivity advantages, driving recent operating margins to 10-12% and GAAP ROIC >30%. However, mechanical contracting is fundamentally project-based; outside peak tech capex cycles, historical margins averaged 5-6% and returns are bounded by competitive general contractor bidding.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC & Pricing Power, REJECT). Comfort Systems has executed brilliantly in modular prefabrication for hyperscale data centers, driving record margins and returns. However, specialty mechanical contracting lacks structural switching costs or barrier-to-entry moats. Project awards remain subject to competitive procurement, and operating margins historically normalized to 5-6% across standard construction cycles, lacking cycle-invariant pricing power.
qualitative.evidence: Revenues scaled rapidly from $2.7B in 2020 to >$6.0B in 2024-2025 with operating margins doubling from ~5.5% to >11% on data center modular construction. However, 10-year through-cycle margins average ~6%, and work is executed under fixed-price or guaranteed maximum price contracts that expose Comfort Systems to input cost inflation and project delay liabilities once hyperscale capex cycles mature.

qualitative.3m: Technical professional services, consulting, and engineering for government infrastructure, water, environmental, and advanced facilities. However, professional consulting contracts are subject to competitive government RFP procurement and corporate budgeting cycles, resulting in thin operating margins (6-8%) and 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 6.2%, well below the 12% hurdle.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, REJECT). Client contracts are routinely re-competed every 3-5 years.

qualitative.3m: North America's largest craft-labor specialty contractor for electric power grids, renewable infrastructure, and telecom. qualitative.evidence: Revenues expanded to >$22B in 2024-2025, but GAAP operating margins remain in the 7.0-8.5% range. 10-year median GAAP ROIC is ~9.5% (GAAP ROIC hovered between 8.5% and 11.5% across 2020-2025). High capital expenditures for specialized utility truck fleets and working capital requirements absorb significant cash flow, preventing excess returns on invested capital.

qualitative.3m: Global engineering professional services consultancy built through continuous M&A rollups (Golder, Wood E&I, Parsons Brinckerhoff). qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12%, REJECT). Organic growth is modest (4-6%), with growth driven by continuous M&A rather than organic pricing power.

General contracting projects face chronic cost-overrun liabilities and thin margins.

qualitative.3m: Global design, engineering, and management consulting for natural and built assets (water, environment, buildings, infrastructure). qualitative.evidence: Net revenues of ~€3.8B with operating EBITA margins of 10.0-10.5%. 5-year median GAAP ROIC is ~10.5%, falling short of the 12% hurdle. Organic growth is tied to municipal and corporate environmental capex budgets where price competition is persistent.

qualitative.3m: General construction and civil engineering contractor operating primarily in the Netherlands, UK, and Ireland. General construction contracting is inherently commoditized and exposed to fixed-price project execution risks, resulting in volatile, low single-digit operating margins (2-4%) and complete absence of an economic moat.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (3a=None, 3b=N, REJECT). Dutch general construction contractor operating in tender-based building and civil engineering markets. Despite restructuring to derisk project portfolios, construction contracting remains a thin-margin commodity business lacking structural pricing power or an economic moat.
qualitative.evidence: Group adjusted EBITDA margins are thin at 4.5-5.5% (operating margins ~2-3%). Construction contracts are awarded on competitive bids where margins are routinely eroded by material and subcontractor inflation. Lacks intellectual property, customer lock-in, or sustainable competitive differentiation.

qualitative.3m: UK-based international infrastructure construction group (civil engineering, rail, construction services, and infrastructure investments). qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (3a=None, 3b=N, REJECT). UK construction contractor operating in low-margin civil engineering and building services. While infrastructure investment concessions generate portfolio cash, general construction operations operate on razor-thin operating margins (~2-3%) without pricing power.
qualitative.evidence: Revenues of ~£9B deliver underlying operating profit of £230M-£250M, reflecting underlying operating margins of only 2.5-2.8%. Construction contracts in the UK and US are subject to competitive public procurement, fixed-price project risks, and labor availability bottlenecks.

qualitative.3m: World's premier concession infrastructure operator. qualitative.evidence: Concessions represent >70% of group EBIT with motorway EBITDA margins >72%. 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 11.7% and tangible operating ROIC exceeds 35% due to long-term concession amortization. Bouygues Telecom faces intense French mobile price competition from Free and Orange, while construction and technical installations operate in highly competitive bidding environments.

[5-10Y g: APRR motorway traffic volume 1.0% + CPI toll escalation 2.5% + energy systems contracting mix 1.5% - concession amortization/tax drag 1.0% + dividend yield 0.0%]

Owner FCF conversion averaged over 200% from 2022 to 2025 (€2.3B+ Owner FCF in FY2025 vs €1.02B Net Income). EBIT/interest coverage is 6.36x, comfortably surpassing the infrastructure concession threshold.

Lacks structural pricing power or an insurmountable competitive barrier.

qualitative.3m: Global construction management and engineering holding company controlling US general builder Turner and Australia's CIMIC, plus an economic interest in Abertis toll motorways. Consolidated net margins of ~2% and competitive project procurement prevent structural pricing power or multi-cycle ROIC >= 12%.
qualitative.evidence: On €33.3B of revenue in FY2024, operational net profit reached €625M (a 1.9% net margin). While Turner benefits from US data center and battery fab demand, general building and civil contracting operate under competitive tender dynamics that structurally limit returns on capital across economic cycles.

qualitative.3m: Infrastructure concession portfolio (>90% of EBITDA) spanning toll highways, hospitals, and water assets, largely underpinned by availability payments or CPI-indexed tariffs with minimal direct demand risk across Spain, Italy, and Latin America.
qualitative.4n: Initial CAP 15Y reduced by -10Y for competitive P3 concession bidding (4_riv=1), Latin American sovereign counterparty exposure (4_buy=1), heavy debt refinancing burden under higher interest rates (4_sup=1), and finite concession lifespans (4_sub=1) yielding Final CAP 5Y.

qualitative.evidence: While concessions generate >90% of EBITDA (€1.35B in 2024) with solid cash conversion, total net debt remains elevated at ~€8.8B against net income of €110-150M. High refinancing sensitivity in an elevated rate environment (Macrotrend 5) combined with Latin American sovereign risk and finite concession durations caps CAP at 5 years.

qualitative.3m: General construction contracting is an inherently commoditized, tender-driven service business characterized by low operating margins (~3.5%) and fixed-price contract overrun risks. Commercial property development is capital-intensive and highly cyclical, suffering sharp writedowns during real estate downturns. The company lacks structural pricing power and fails to achieve a 12% multi-cycle GAAP ROIC.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3 (3a=None, 3b=N, REJECT). Skanska operates as a general construction contractor and commercial property developer in the Nordics, Europe, and the US. Construction contracting is a tender-driven commodity business with thin operating margins (~3.5%), while commercial property development is cyclical with periodic portfolio impairments, failing the 12% multi-cycle ROIC moat threshold.
qualitative.evidence: Construction operating margins consistently hovered around ~3.3-3.5% between 2020 and 2024. Commercial Property Development ROCE collapsed to 2.6% in 2024 and was negative in 2023 due to commercial real estate devaluations in the US and Europe. Consolidated through-cycle ROIC falls well short of the 12% hurdle.

qualitative.3m: Local technician density and long-term facility maintenance contracts create moderate customer stickiness across electrical, mechanical, and HVAC technical services. However, switching barriers are not prohibitive, contracts are subject to periodic corporate procurement rebidding, and operating EBITA margins of ~6-7% reflect competitive market conditions rather than proprietary pricing power.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% & Pricing Power, REJECT). European multi-technical services provider benefiting from energy transition and building decarbonization electrification. qualitative.evidence: 5-year median GAAP ROIC is ~10.4% (operating EBITA margins 6.0-6.8%). While cash conversion is strong due to asset-light operations, pricing power is limited by enterprise procurement tenders, and serial bolt-on M&A creates an expanding goodwill base.

qualitative.3m: Proprietary engineering technologies and project delivery track record in liquefied natural gas (LNG), hydrogen, and ethylene. Despite strong market share in modular LNG, project-based engineering contracting is exposed to severe energy capex cyclicality, fixed-price project execution liabilities, and customer bargaining power, failing the durable economic moat test.
qualitative.evidence: Operating margins range from 6% to 8% on project deliveries. While tangible ROIC appears inflated by substantial customer advance payments and net cash, group revenues and earnings are lumpy and heavily reliant on mega-project awards (e.g. Qatar North Field). Lacks recurring toll-booth revenue or insurmountable customer lock-in.

qualitative.evidence: Consolidated operating margins range between 8% and 11% across freight cycles. OEM truck makers (Paccar, Daimler Truck) increasingly develop proprietary engines, capping Cummins' long-term pricing power and volume.

PACCAR Financial carries substantial debt to finance customer truck purchases, exposing the business to credit cycle fluctuations.

qualitative.3m: Locomotive manufacturing and freight rail braking systems, positive train control (PTC), and digital solutions.
